scene.bubble: Words have power. Learn how prefixes and suffixes build meaning — and how adverts use them.
scene.intro: For the Inspiring Nordic project, our group looked at advertisements and discovered how powerful words can be. In this unit you read about the words that change our minds, you learn how prefixes and suffixes build new words, and you write your own honest advert. One small ending can change everything: 'use' becomes 'useful' or 'useless'. Let's learn to use word power well.

data.title: The words that change your mind
data.author: mateo
data.text:
For the Inspiring Nordic project, our group studied advertisements — and we discovered how powerful words can be. A good advert doesn't just describe a product; it changes how you feel about it.

Look at the words companies choose. A drink is not just 'nice'; it is 'refreshing' and 'natural'. A phone is 'powerful' and 'unbelievable'. Even a boring product becomes 'useful' and 'comfortable'. These words are built from smaller parts: 'use' becomes 'useful' or 'useless', and 'comfort' becomes 'comfortable'. One small ending can change everything.

Advertisers also use words that create feelings. 'Happiness', 'freedom' and 'success' are not things you can touch, but they sound wonderful. Sometimes the words are almost dishonest: an 'unmissable offer' or an 'impossible price'.

Our teacher warned us to be careful. She said that a careful reader is never fooled by clever language. If you understand how words are built, you understand the message behind them.

For our project posters, we decided to use word power honestly. We want to persuade people to value real skills — and that is a message worth spreading with the right words.

data.title: Word formation: prefixes and suffixes
data.intro: We build new words by adding parts. A prefix goes before a word; a suffix goes after. They change the meaning or the type of word.
rules: -ness makes a noun from an adjective: happy → happiness, kind → kindness.
Prefixes un-, im-, dis- make the opposite: unhappy, impossible, disagree.

items.sentence: This tool is very ___. It helps a lot.
He never listens; he is so ___.
The whole class felt great ___ when we won.
Sorry, that is ___. We can't do it.
I ___ with you. I think you're wrong.

data.voice_note: Voz: la profesora (Miss Vega), cerrando el proyecto de anuncios.
data.script: Good morning, Grade 8. Today we finish our advertisement project. Remember three things about word power. First, adjectives like 'powerful' and 'amazing' create strong feelings. Second, be careful with words like 'free' and 'unmissable' — they are often tricks. Third, a suffix can change a word completely: 'use' becomes 'useful'. For homework, choose one advert and find five powerful words. Bring your list on Monday!

activities.title: Speaking — persuade with words. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: In pairs, invent a short advert for a school product (a pencil, a chair, a book club). Use powerful, positive words: useful, amazing, comfortable, unmissable… Try to persuade your partner, then swap. Record your best advert.

homework.prompt: Write a short, honest advert (5–7 sentences) for the Inspiring Nordic project — a real school skill or club you believe in. Use word power: at least four words with prefixes or suffixes (useful, powerful, kindness, impossible…). Persuade honestly. Capital letters and full stops!
